[erdos_gyarfas] DFS depth-chain discharging (ideation rank 2, score 30/40). In a hypothetical counterexample, back-edge depth-gaps are forbidden in {3,7,15,31,...} and two back edges at one vertex with gaps d1<d2 forbid d2-d1 in {2,6,14,30,...}; min degree 3 forces every DFS leaf to carry >=2 back edges, making leaves charge sources; seek a sub-invariance inequality showing ancestor chains cannot absorb the redistributed charge (the von-Mangoldt-on-chains shape that closed Erdos #1196; face-based Heckman-Krakovski discharging is intrinsically planar, depth-chains are not). First lemma (killable): pairwise chain-locality -- for connected min-degree-3 graphs on <=12 vertices and any DFS tree, some power-of-2 cycle is a fundamental cycle or a symmetric difference of two fundamental cycles. Judge condition: expand the CHECK probe from 4 named graphs to ALL connected min-degree-3 graphs on <=10 vertices, and handle the caveat that a symmetric difference of two fundamental cycles is only a simple cycle under an edge-disjointness/nesting condition.

[frankl_union_closed] KL union deficiency -- entropy beyond the Chase-Lovett barrier (ideation rank 1, score 35/40). Exact union-closure means T: mu -> law(A u B) maps distributions on F to distributions ON F, so the deficiency D(law(A u B) || Unif(F)) = log|F| - H(A u B) >= 0 is well-defined slack that literally does not exist for Chase-Lovett approximate families. Plan: lower-bound the deficiency by an explicit decreasing phi(p) of max element frequency p, rerun the AHS/Sawin entropy computation with H(A u B) <= log|F| - phi(p) to shift the 0.382 fixed point upward; iterate T (unions of unions stay in F) to telescope deficiencies toward 1/2; compatible with Sawin-style dependent couplings. First lemma (killable, quantitative): log2|F| - H(A u B) >= (1-p)^2/4 bits for A,B iid uniform on F. Judge condition: stress the constant with adversarial exact families with p in [0.382, 0.45) (e.g. Chase-Lovett-style families forced exact by closure), since power sets pass with wide margin. Predicted true obstacle: exact families with p just above 0.382 whose union distribution asymptotically flattens (D -> 0).

[frankl_union_closed] Transitive-symmetry counterexample screen (ideation rank 3, score 30/40, queued as the cheap orthogonal disproof arm). A transitive automorphism group equalizes all element frequencies, collapsing 'every frequency < 1/2' to one scalar: average member size < n/2. Screen union-closures of group orbits -- cyclic shifts first, then dihedral/affine/PSL(2,q) -- with 1-3 generator sets of density ~0.35-0.40 (Chase-Lovett hint) at n = 13..64, keeping |closure| <= 5000 to fit the witness verifier; any hit is an instant verified witness, and uniform failure plus the union-cascade heuristic points to a provable no-transitive-counterexample pruning lemma. First lemma (maximally killable, fully decided per n): for nonempty A subset Z_n, the union-closure of the cyclic orbit of A has average member size >= n/2; exhaustive sweep n = 4..10 over generators of size 2-4.
